The Routing Information Protocol (RIP) is an intradomain routing protocol used inside an Autonomous System (AS).
Based on Distance Vector Routing.
Metric in RIP is called a hop count, which represents the number of links or networks to reach the destination.
The number of networks that must be traversed to reach the destination is called the hop count.
The path with the least hops is considered the optimal route to a network.
Max hop count = 15.
Infinity is defined as 16, which means that any route in an AS using RIP cannot have more than 15 hops.
If hop count = 16, the network is considered inaccessible.

Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) is an intradomain routing protocol based on link state routing.
OSPF operates as an Interior Gateway Protocol within an Autonomous System.
Metric in OSPF is defined as Cost, which accounts for minimum delay and maximum throughput.
A transient link is a network with several routers attached to it where data can enter through any router and leave through any router.
A stub link is a network that is connected to only one router, where data packets enter and leave through the same router.
A point-to-point link connects two routers without any other host or router in between.
